summary: Paul Tedesco worked in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. After studying philology at the University of Vienna (1916–1921), he held research and faculty posts at Princeton (~1944–1952) and Yale University (1943, 1952, and 1960–1966).

Paul Thieme worked in Indology and linguistics. He earned his PhD and habilitation at Göttingen and also studied at Berlin and Allahabad. He held professorships at Halle-Wittenberg (1941–1953), Frankfurt (1953), Yale (1954–1960), and Tübingen (1960–1973; emeritus 1975).

Paul Tillich was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied at Berlin, Tübingen, Halle-Wittenberg, and Breslau (PhD 1910). His professorships included TU Dresden (1925–1929), Frankfurt (1929–1933), Union Theological Seminary (1933–1955), Harvard (1955–1962), and Chicago (1962–1965).

Paul W. Kroll is a Sinologist who studied at the University of Michigan (~1971–1976). He served at the University of Colorado as Associate Professor of Chinese and department chair (~1979) and later as a Faculty Fellow (attested 2001).

Paul Williams is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his BA at Sussex and DPhil at Oxford. He served as a fellow at Wadham College and held the post of Professor of Indian and Tibetan Philosophy at Bristol (~1980–2011).

Paul de Lagarde worked in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and religious studies. He studied at Berlin under Friedrich Rückert and at Halle-Wittenberg, later holding posts at Halle-Wittenberg (~1851–1854) and the University of Göttingen (~1869–1891).

Paula Arai specializes in Buddhist, religious, and Japanese studies. She studied at Kalamazoo College, Waseda, and Harvard (PhD 1993). She held posts at Vanderbilt (1994–2002), Louisiana State University (2007), and the Institute of Buddhist Studies (2023).

Paulinus of St. Bartholomew was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Collegio San Pancrazio (~1771–1774). He served at the Malabar Mission (1776–1789) and in 1800 became inspector of studies at the Pontifical Urban University and counsellor to the Congregation of the Index.

Pe Maung Tin worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. Educated at Rangoon, Calcutta, and Oxford, he served at the University of Rangoon as Professor of Pali (1912) and principal (1937–1946), and later as principal of the University of Adult Education (1947).
Pedro Manuel Castro Sánchez is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Peter Harvey and completed an MA at the University of Sunderland.

Pei-jung Wu is a scholar of history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She earned a BA from National Taiwan University and completed her PhD at UCLA in 2002 under Donald F. McCallum, also studying under Hironobu Kohara, Shou-chien Shih, and Yu-min Lee.

Pema Bhum is a Tibetologist who served as a professor of Tibetan languages and letters at Lanzhou University and Indiana University, and as Director of the Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library (attested 2003–2009).

Pema Chödrön is a Buddhist studies practitioner educated at Sarah Lawrence and UC Berkeley. She studied under Chime Tulku Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Chögyam Trungpa, serving as director of the Boulder Shambhala Center (~1979–1984) and abbess and director at Gampo Abbey.
Pema Kunzang Tendzin was a Tibetan scholar who studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Pema Tekchok Loden was a Tibetan scholar who studied under Shechen Gyaltsab, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Khenpo Shenga.
Pema Tekchok Tenpai Gyeltsen studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He also taught Shechen Gyaltsab and Khenpo Shenga.
Pema Tsering is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Khenpo Shenga, taught Ruth Gamble, and held an attested post at the University of Bonn in 1996.
Pema Vajra 01 studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Khenpo Shenga, and taught Shechen Gyaltsab, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Pema Wangchok Gyelpo studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, Khakyab Dorje, and Khenpo Shenga. He also taught Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Khenpo Shenga.

Penghao Sun specializes in Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Leonard van der Kuijp as doctoral supervisor, Qingying Chen (2009–2011), Weirong Shen, Mark Elliott, Charles Hallisey, Peter K. Bol, Jay Jasanoff, James Robson, Ryuichi Abe, and Jie Li.
